The issue was stale VASP reports surviving across calculations. When a previous calculation was copied for restart, its uncompressed `vasprun.xml` remained in the working directory. The archived runner then supplied the current report in compressed form, but the parser preferred the stale uncompressed report, so every deformation reused the tight-relaxation stress and produced an effectively zero elastic response.

The repair in [source/src/atomate2/vasp/jobs/base.py](/workspace/task/source/src/atomate2/vasp/jobs/base.py) removes prior calculation reports—both compressed and uncompressed—after restart/input preparation and before running/parsing the new calculation. Restart artifacts such as wavefunctions and charge densities are preserved.

Verification:

- `python reproduce.py` completes successfully with `workflow_completed`.
- Archived deformation stresses are now distinct and match the supplied VASP reports.
- The fitted silicon tensor is finite and physically nonzero:
  - \(C_{11}\) ≈ 155.79 GPa
  - \(C_{12}\) ≈ 54.89 GPa
  - \(C_{44}\) ≈ 31.54 GPa in IEEE format
  - \(K_\mathrm{VRH}\) ≈ 88.52 GPa
  - \(G_\mathrm{VRH}\) ≈ 38.10 GPa
- The IEEE tensor has positive eigenvalues.
- Source compilation and diff validation pass.
- Supplied scientific inputs and generated reports were not modified.
